attributes.description: Optional user attributes for offer selection

age.description: Whole years, as an integer. If you hold only a RANGE, send its LOWEST end: "13-17" is sent as 13. Under 18 restricts this request to offers rated for that age, with no per-user personalisation. Used for this request and never stored on the user. When the user is 18 or over, the app is not child-directed and the request carries no opt-out of personalisation, Encore keeps the age in whole years in its serve log for this request and deletes it on a data-subject erasure request; otherwise it is never stored or logged. Lower than an age stored through /users/attributes, it wins; higher, the stored one does. A fraction is rounded down, also as a decimal string ("17.9" is 17), a whole-number string is read as its number, and a range string as its lowest end ("13-17" is 13, "65+" is 65); any other value is ignored, never a 400.

dateOfBirth.description: Deprecated: send age instead. A YYYY-MM-DD date, or an ISO 8601 date-time with a zone, is turned into an age for this request, then discarded: the date is never stored or logged, and the age follows the rules for age. If age is also sent, the younger of the two is used. An unreadable date is ignored, never a 400.

language.description: BCP 47 language tag; only the language subtag is used for creative locale resolution, and only when the app has that language enabled. Falls back to Accept-Language, then the app default locale.

requestId.description: Session ID for deterministic pagination - if not provided, server will generate one

platform.description: Client platform: android, ios, or web

variantId.description: SDUI variant ID from frontend config fetch. If provided, filters creatives by variant assignment. If not provided, no variant filtering is applied.

placementId.description: Publisher-defined surface label for where the offer is shown (e.g. 'paywall', 'onboarding', 'settings'). Stamped onto the sdk_offer_requested event so publisher analytics can break the funnel out by placement. An Encore admin can also configure a per-placement offer rule for an app, in which case this label SELECTS and ORDERS the offers returned for that placement; with no rule configured, which is the default for every app, it stays analytics-only and changes nothing about what is served. Max 64 chars. SDKs may send their own auto-generated `placement_<8 hex>` id when the publisher supplied none — that is expected and is folded into the '(unlabeled)' bucket at read time; do NOT substitute '(unlabeled)' or an empty string yourself.

useCase.description: Which Encore surface is being filled. Ignored while OFFERS_SEARCH_RESOLVES_SURFACE is off. With it on and no variantId, the server resolves the variant for this use case (and the placementId pin) as GET /config does; a sent variantId always wins. Absent or unrecognised: today's behaviour (churn-intervention). Never a 400.

maxPostbackTimeMs.description: Strict unlock mode: only include campaigns whose postback latency is less than or equal to this value (in milliseconds). Omit for no filtering. Bounded 1000..120000.

publisherRewardDailyLimit.description: Send only when this placement carries the app's own prize for a reward-for-trying Yes: the app's daily prize limit from its SDK configuration (PublisherRewardPolicy), clamped server-side to 1..10. The response then carries publisherRewardPromise. Omit it and nothing changes.

purpose.description: Why the client is searching. `purpose: "prefetch"` marks a search the SDK runs before any sheet is shown (a GiftsButton or ClaimReminder checking that offers exist). Its result may later back the sheet the user opens with a tap, so it is a served request like any other, not an impression. It is stamped as purpose on sdk_offer_requested so a report can split these out. Any other value is ignored, never a 400. Serving is identical either way.

context.description: Request-scoped serving context. Unknown keys are ignored.

activity.description: Request-scoped activity the user is engaged in at serve time (what the surface is being used for, not a persisted user property). Recognized values: laundry, vending, car_wash, air_vacuum, amusement. Any other value is accepted and recorded on serve analytics, so unrecognized activities show up in reporting rather than failing the request. Does not change which offers are served today.

shareUrl.description: Opaque link a user can send to someone else for this campaign. A claim made through it attributes back to the user who shared it. MUST be absolute and http or https: both SDKs drop anything else while parsing, so a scheme-less or relative value reads as absent and no share control is drawn. ABSENT until share links ship, and a client that finds it absent must share nothing rather than falling back to another URL: an unattributed link loses the claim the share exists to carry. /offers/search only. Deliberately a plain string, not `format: uri`: that format makes the Kotlin generator emit java.net.URI, and a link its parser rejects would fail the WHOLE offers decode on Android rather than just the share button.

category.description: Display name of the campaign category, e.g. "Music and Audio". Free string: the taxonomy is admin-editable, so accept any value.

categoryGroup.description: The gift-sheet group this campaign files under: "Watch & listen", "Money" or "Everyday". Derived from `category` by the server so a native chip strip shows what web tabs show without holding the taxonomy map. Always set: an absent, blank or unmapped category files under "Everyday", so every offer sits in some group. Whether a strip is worth drawing is the client's call, because only it knows which offers its sheet lists. /offers/search only: web-sdk holds its own copy of the map and groups `category` itself.

categoryDisplayName.description: `category` in the response locale, for display only. Group and filter on `category`, which stays English. Null when `category` is null. /offers/search only.

categoryGroupDisplayName.description: `categoryGroup` in the response locale, for display only. Group on `categoryGroup`, which stays English. /offers/search only.

rewardConfirmationTime.description: Estimated time from the user tapping this offer to the reward being confirmed, from recent real conversions (on demo offers, from the demo advertiser's configured behavior instead). Half confirm within medianSeconds, 9 in 10 within p90Seconds. Not a guarantee: to show a wait, use p90Seconds. Null when there is no current estimate (too few recent conversions, data more than 7 days old, or an offer that does not confirm through the advertiser); say nothing about timing then.

selfReported.description: When true, this user already answered Yes on the reward-for-trying question for this offer and has not completed it. The offer is still served (only a completed offer is withheld), but a second Yes never earns the app's prize again, so promise none on it. Absent or false otherwise.

publisherRewardPromise.description: Whether this user is still under the app's daily prize limit (publisherRewardDailyLimit, rolling 24 hours). What counts depends on publisherRewardMode. on_yes (or no mode): prizes granted on a reward-for-trying Yes. on_verified: this user's verified completions that carried a reward, by when they verified; a Yes never grants and never counts, and the reward arrives on the offer_completed webhook. Present only when the request sent publisherRewardDailyLimit. Offers this user already completed are never served. An offer this user already said Yes to is served with selfReported true and never earns again, whatever this says. Absent (an older backend, or no limit sent) means no promise. Not a grant: in on_yes the self-report's granted answer is final.

post.description: Rebrokering catalog: the full set of offers your app may serve to a given end user, to render on your own surface. Two hard, server-enforced filters always apply: entitlement (your app's opt-outs + whitelist) and geo (offers not redeemable in the end user's country are dropped: non-redeemable offers are never returned). Serve path requires `userId` (a stable end-user identifier) and geo (`countryCode`, or the end user's IP forwarded via X-Forwarded-For); missing either is a 400. On the serve path, offers this end user already completed (a brand-confirmed conversion, theirs or carried over at identify) are left out. An offer they only said Yes to through an Encore SDK is still returned. Each returned creative carries a tokenized `clickUrl`: route the end user there on tap and it records an attributed transaction (bound to your app, the offer, the creative, and the userId) then 302s to the advertiser. Filter to your curated offer IDs and order CLIENT-SIDE, falling back to other returned offers so your surface is never empty (the server does not narrow to your picks). Set `includeAllRegions: true` for config-time discovery of your full addressable inventory (skips geo, needs no userId, returns no clickUrls; each offer carries targetCountries); not for display. Authentication: publishable key (X-API-Key: pk_live_* / pk_test_*).

userId.description: Stable identifier for the END USER you are rendering offers to (any opaque string; does not need to be PII). REQUIRED on the serve path — it is bound into each offer's clickUrl so a click records a transaction attributed to (your app, the offer, the creative, this user), it drives per-user fraud controls (trial caps, retake blocking) at click time, and on the serve path it leaves out offers this user already completed. Use the same value across renders for the same user. Not required when includeAllRegions is set (config mode returns no clickUrls).

clientId.description: Optional identifier for the operator/sub-publisher on whose behalf offers are shown. Carried through as an analytics dimension. Defaults to userId when omitted.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the END USER the offers will be shown to (e.g. "US", "GB"). Provides the geography signal for geo-filtering. Resolution: this value → client IP (X-Forwarded-For aware) → (rejected if neither resolves). Send it when calling server-to-server without forwarding the end user's IP; omit it when the end user (or a proxy forwarding their IP) is the caller. Ignored when includeAllRegions is true.

platform.description: Optional device family of the END USER the offers will be shown to (enum; any other value is rejected with 400). Analytics dimension only (platform on the serve event); never 'api'.

placementId.description: Optional publisher-defined label for the surface this offer is shown on (e.g. 'cancel_flow', 'home_feed', 'post_purchase'). Stamped onto the impression AND onto the click it produces, so publisher analytics can break the funnel out by placement. Normalised server-side: a blank value is treated as absent, anything longer than 64 characters is TRUNCATED rather than rejected, and the stored label NEVER carries leading or trailing whitespace, including after truncation, so ' my label ' and 'my label' are always one placement and can never show up as two rows. Case IS significant: 'Cancel_Flow' and 'cancel_flow' are different placements. Omit it and this traffic groups under '(unlabeled)', the same bucket as an SDK integration that supplies no placement. A per-placement offer rule NEVER applies here. `/offers/catalog` returns inventory rather than a served set, so a rule configured for this label does not select or order what comes back. Scope an inventory pull on your own filters, never on a rule.

language.description: Optional BCP 47 language tag (e.g. "es", "pt-BR"), from the host's language override. Wins over Accept-Language; only the language subtag is used (nb is served as no; iw, in, ji, jw as he, id, yi, jv), and only when the app has it enabled, else Accept-Language, then the app default. A tag the SDKs would refuse (malformed, underscores, or an extended language subtag such as zh-yue-HK) is 400 with details.code INVALID_LANGUAGE.

includeAllRegions.description: CONFIG-TIME ONLY. When true, skips geo-filtering and returns the full addressable inventory for your app (entitlement still applies), with each offer's targetCountries — use this to build your curation. Do NOT use for offers displayed to an end user; those must come from a geo-scoped request (countryCode or forwarded IP). When true, no geography signal is required and countryCode is ignored.

limit.description: Optional page size (1..100). OMIT to return ALL eligible offers (the default) — catalogs are small enough that you normally take the whole set and curate client-side. Provide only if you want to page (with offset).

offset.description: Pagination offset (default 0). Only meaningful together with limit.

includeOffersWithoutImage.description: Opt in to offers whose campaign has no ad creative. Default false: you only get offers with a creative, as before. When true, such an offer still has a headline, an image and a click link: on /offers/feed and /offers/message its imageUrl is the offer hero image, else the campaign logo, else the advertiser logo (a logo is often square, not a banner), additionalImages is empty, and title is the offer title or else the perk. On /offers/catalog it has creatives: [] and, on the serve path, its own offer-level clickUrl.

post.description: DEPRECATED (2026-08-24): kept serving for existing integrators; new integrations use /offers/feed. Select one eligible offer for a third-party messaging surface (WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram) and return the raw offer fields, the branded short clickUrl plus context (title, description, imageUrl, advertiserName, perk), so the integrator composes their own message. Calling this endpoint is NOT itself the impression: it emits sdk_offer_requested and returns impressionUid; confirm display via POST /offers/impressions/{impressionUid}/delivered once the message is delivered. Authentication: publishable key (X-API-Key: pk_live_* / pk_test_*). Retries are NOT deduplicated server-side (no retry-stable client key on the request), so each call produces a distinct short link and analytics row.

clientId.description: Stable identifier for the integrator-client (the business / operator the message is being sent on behalf of). Carried through as an analytics dimension so impressions, clicks, and conversions can be broken down per client.

chatId.description: Conversation / thread identifier on the messaging platform. Used as the messaging-surface userId — drives bandit seeding for `/offers/message`, the transaction created at click time, and the userId dimension on the click event.

language.description: BCP 47 language tag; only the language subtag is used for creative locale resolution, and only when the app has that language enabled. Falls back to Accept-Language, then the app default locale.

platform.description: Recipient's device platform; it drives creative compatibility filtering. Send it whenever you know the end user's device, so they only get offers that run there and the impression is recorded under that platform. Omit it only when the device is unknown: a platform='api' app then gets offers picked with no platform trimming. Device-SDK apps always send it. 'api' is not a valid value here.

osVersion.description: Device OS version, e.g. '14' or '17.5.1'. Optional; a malformed value is ignored.

userAgent.description: The END DEVICE's user agent, not the caller's. On the API lane the publisher's server calls us, so the header we see is theirs. Optional; a malformed value is ignored.

advertisingId.description: Device advertising id, unhashed: IDFA on iOS, GAID/GPID on Android. Optional, and accepted only from an app whose `deviceIdentifiersMode` is enabled and which is not declared for children or likely used by them; ignored otherwise. Must be a UUID; an all-zero id reads as absent.

limitAdTracking.description: True when the user has limited ad tracking. Accepts OpenRTB's 0/1 integer too. A consent signal, not a device attribute. Optional; a malformed value counts as true.

doNotTrack.description: OpenRTB `device.dnt`. A consent signal like `limitAdTracking`, and equally underivable. Accepts 0/1 too. Optional; a malformed value counts as true.

deviceIp.description: Public IPv4 or IPv6 address of the END DEVICE, never your server's. Same gate as `advertisingId`. Optional; a malformed, private or reserved address is ignored.

gdprApplies.description: OpenRTB `regs.gdpr`: true when GDPR applies to this user. Accepts 0/1 too. Optional; a malformed value counts as true.

consentString.description: IAB TCF consent string from your consent tool, forwarded as `user.consent`. Optional; a malformed value is ignored.

gpp.description: IAB Global Privacy Platform string, forwarded as `regs.gpp`. Optional; a malformed value counts as an opt-out.

gppSid.description: GPP section ids in force, forwarded as `regs.gpp_sid`. Optional; a malformed value counts as an opt-out.

usPrivacy.description: IAB US Privacy string, e.g. '1YNN', forwarded as `regs.us_privacy`. Optional; a malformed value counts as an opt-out.

attributes.description: Targeting attributes. countryCode and language are required; send platform whenever you know the end user's device (a platform='api' app that omits it gets one offer picked with no platform trimming).

placementId.description: Optional publisher-defined label for the surface this offer is shown on (e.g. 'cancel_flow', 'home_feed', 'post_purchase'). Stamped onto the impression AND onto the click it produces, so publisher analytics can break the funnel out by placement. Normalised server-side: a blank value is treated as absent, anything longer than 64 characters is TRUNCATED rather than rejected, and the stored label NEVER carries leading or trailing whitespace, including after truncation, so ' my label ' and 'my label' are always one placement and can never show up as two rows. Case IS significant: 'Cancel_Flow' and 'cancel_flow' are different placements. Omit it and this traffic groups under '(unlabeled)', the same bucket as an SDK integration that supplies no placement. An Encore admin can also configure a per-placement offer rule for an app, in which case this label SELECTS and ORDERS the offers returned for that placement; with no rule configured, which is the default for every app, it stays analytics-only and changes nothing about what is served.

includeOffersWithoutImage.description: Opt in to offers whose campaign has no ad creative. Default false: you only get offers with a creative, as before. When true, such an offer still has a headline, an image and a click link: on /offers/feed and /offers/message its imageUrl is the offer hero image, else the campaign logo, else the advertiser logo (a logo is often square, not a banner), additionalImages is empty, and title is the offer title or else the perk. On /offers/catalog it has creatives: [] and, on the serve path, its own offer-level clickUrl.

impressionUid.description: Handle for the served offer; POST /offers/impressions/{impressionUid}/delivered when the message is confirmed delivered to the user (that call is the impression). Absent when no offer was served.

placementId.description: Optional publisher-defined label for the surface this offer is shown on (e.g. 'cancel_flow', 'home_feed', 'post_purchase'). post.description: Record that the user answered "Yes, I completed it" to a reward-for-trying offer, and decide whether the app may grant its own prize. Send it on EVERY tapped Yes, prize or not: the Yes is stored per person (the app's user id), so a later Yes on the same offer never earns again, including after a reinstall or on a second device. A Yes never hides the offer or refuses a re-claim: only a completion does. granted is true only for the first Yes per person per offer, while the person is under the app's daily limit (a rolling 24 hours). Treat no answer as no prize. Idempotent on reportId. Never changes the transaction: no status, payout, entitlement or webhook. 404 when the transaction does not belong to this app, or userId is not the current user id of the person who claimed it. This route does not distinguish an identified user from an SDK-generated anonymous id: an app that wants prizes kept to signed-in users must gate the promise client-side.

userId.description: The SDK's CURRENT user id at the moment the report is sent (not the id captured when the user tapped Yes). Must equal the current app user id of the user who owns the transaction, or the request is a 404.

reportId.description: Minted once per tapped Yes and reused on every retry of that Yes, with the same body. A retry gets the same granted. On a refused Yes the server keeps only that no prize was granted, so the retry's reason is derived from the retry's own body (daily_cap when it carries publisherRewardId, else no_prize): resend the body unchanged.

publisherRewardId.description: Present only when a prize was promised for this Yes. Absent: the Yes is still recorded (a later Yes on this offer never earns) and granted is false with reason no_prize.

dailyLimit.description: The app's daily prize limit from its SDK configuration. Required when publisherRewardId is present. Clamped server-side to 1..10.

granted.description: Whether the app may grant its prize for this Yes. True only for the first Yes per person per offer, under the daily limit. The ONLY source of prize eligibility: no answer (timeout, offline, 5xx, 404) means no prize.

reportedAt.description: When the server recorded this person's Yes for this offer (the first one, on a retry or a second device).

get.description: Get unified SDK configuration including SDUI, entitlements, experiments, and remote config. This endpoint replaces /ui-config with a cleaner structure. Entitlement mode is implicit: if entitlements.iap.productId exists, use IAP mode; otherwise use Native mode. Pass `useCase` to configure a surface other than churn-intervention; the response echoes it as ui.useCase. `demoVariant` names an SDUI variant to serve for this request. It is honoured on a TEST key (pk_test_*) for any app, and on a live key only for Encore's own demo apps; for every other app it is ignored silently (never an error). It exists for demos and previews: Encore's own demo pages, and a publisher who wants to see the other variants against their own test key. `placementId` selects a variant an admin pinned to that placement, in `ui` only; any label without a pin resolves as before. `trigger` makes this a trigger component request (GiftsButton, ClaimReminder): `useCase` is then required and is the real use case it serves, `layout` pins a look and `autoOpen=off` opts the mount out of looks that open the sheet by itself (any other present value also reads as off); a missing useCase or a malformed trigger or layout is a 400. Without `trigger`, `layout` and `autoOpen` are ignored. Requesting a surface is all it takes to be served it — no setup call is required. A surface Encore has explicitly switched off for this app, or one with no variant available, returns ui.template: null — clients must no-op, never reuse another use case's template.

parameters.name: sdkVersion
parameters.description: SDK version for compatibility filtering

parameters.name: language

parameters.name: useCase
parameters.description: Which Encore surface is being configured. Omit for today's behaviour. Requesting a surface is all it takes to be served it — no setup call is required. A surface Encore has explicitly switched off for this app, or one with no variant available, resolves to template: null — it NEVER falls back to another use case's template.

parameters.name: demoVariant
parameters.description: Demos and previews only. The SDUI variant file stem to serve for this request, e.g. 'giftUnwrap'. Honoured on a TEST key (pk_test_*) for any app. On a live key it is honoured only for Encore's own demo apps; for every other app it is ignored silently and resolution is unchanged, never an error. On a trigger request with autoOpen=off, an honoured look that opens the sheet by itself is served with behavior.autoOpen 'off'. Intended for Encore's internal demos and for a publisher previewing the other variants against their own test key. An honoured value bypasses app targeting, experiments and arm weights, and WIDENS the status filter from 'active' to 'active' or 'valid' — the filter is widened, not removed, so a draft, testing, invalid or archived variant is still refused. The use-case partition, the per-app kill switch and the SDK version gate all still apply. Note that a test key also serves the demo campaign catalog rather than live advertiser inventory, and tags the request as test traffic in analytics.

parameters.name: trigger
parameters.description: Present = a trigger component request (GiftsButton, ClaimReminder, customClaim): the camelCase trigger id, e.g. 'giftsButton'. Absent = a sheet request, unchanged. `useCase` is then REQUIRED and names the real use case the trigger serves (a missing useCase or a malformed trigger is a 400). The response's `ui.template` is that trigger's config (`ui.template.trigger` equals this id) or null, and `ui.useCase` echoes the requested use case. Its `root` is an SDUI element tree the SDK draws inline at `root`'s `style.frame.height` (the trigger's height), filling `${...}` from `ui.template.strings` and host values. customClaim (the custom-UI handle, which draws the app's own view) is answered with a rules-only look: layout 'behavior', no `root` or strings, minimal `ui.values`. `ui.template.behavior` names the look's step rules; `behavior.autoOpen` 'on' (an experiment arm only) opens the sheet once by itself, then draws the same look. A holdout carries `ui.experimentId` beside a null template, and `useCases` is always empty.

parameters.name: layout
parameters.description: Trigger requests only (ignored otherwise): pin the look, a camelCase layout name such as 'card' or 'pill' (malformed = 400). Serves the trigger's variant file marked pin for that layout, never enrolls in an experiment, and returns template null when there is none.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Trigger requests only (ignored otherwise): what happened on the device. 'claimOpen' = an eligible open claim; 'completed' = an offer finished on this local day, none claimed since, its thanks not tapped. The served look's behavior then picks the step's look: claimOpen on a gifts button whose behavior.afterClaim is showReminder is answered with the reminder look (ui.template.trigger claimReminder); completed applies behavior.afterComplete (gifts serves the look, hide serves template null, thanks serves the trigger's thanks look). post.description:
Store targeting attributes against a user, ahead of opening the hosted offer page, so the page URL carries only apiKey and userId instead of the attributes themselves. A URL is written into webview history and into hosting access logs and cannot be unwritten.

MERGE. Each call merges into the stored set: a key you send replaces the stored value, a key you omit is kept, and `null` deletes the stored key. `custom` is one key: sending it replaces the whole stored `custom` object. The one exception: `null` does not delete a stored age under 18. Send a corrected age, or use a data-subject erasure request. No expiry: the set stays until a later write changes it or an erasure request removes it.

Precedence: an attribute sent on an /offers/search or /offers/feed request always WINS over the stored one. The stored set only fills an attribute the request omits.

LANGUAGE is accepted and ignored: it is never stored. The hosted page and the SDKs send it on each request, else Accept-Language decides.

AGE. Send `age` as a whole-number integer. If you hold only a RANGE, send its LOWEST end: "13-17" is sent as 13, never 15 and never 17. Sending the middle of a range defeats the under-age check: flooring can never mask a minor, a midpoint can. An age below 18 restricts that user to age-appropriate inventory ranked by the app-level bandit, with NO per-user personalisation; offers are still served. For such a user only `age` and `countryCode` are STORED, the attributes that decide where an offer may legally appear. Every other key, stored or sent, is dropped, `custom` included, and the response reports `minor`. The instant the age was sent is recorded, so a stored age is aged forward rather than frozen. `dateOfBirth` is refused: `age` carries the same targeting value with far less identifying power.

GATED KEYS. email, firstName, lastName, mobile, phoneNumber, postcode, postalCode, latitude, longitude and gender are stored ONLY for an app whose audience is declared adults_only (store-rated 18+). From any other app they are dropped and the rest of the write is stored; the call does not fail. city, state and region are dropped for an app declared child_directed. `age` is NOT gated: it is accepted from any app, because it restricts what a user is shown rather than identifying them. Unrecognised keys are refused with 400 rather than ignored. Authentication: publishable key (X-API-Key: pk_live_* / pk_test_*).

It restricts them to inventory appropriate to their age, ranked by the app-level bandit, with no per-user personalisation. Do not send a date of birth; it is refused. post.description: Mint the creator's shareable affiliate links: one stable branded short link per campaign your app is entitled to serve (every enabled campaign, regardless of geo). Idempotent — the same creatorId always returns the same link per campaign. Each link is a single URL clickable by many people; every distinct click is an independent claim tracked as its own transaction. Authentication: publishable key (X-API-Key: pk_live_* / pk_test_*).

amount.description: Publisher's payout per completion: campaign payout × the app's payout split (raw campaign payout when no split is set).

model.description: Campaign payout model (CPA / CPC / CPI / CPM).

categories.description: The campaign's categories (for offer-wall filter tabs). Empty when the campaign has none.

supportedPlatforms.description: Platforms this creative supports (empty = all platforms)

get.description: Real-time performance for a creator's links, per campaign and per day: clicks (each click = one claim), completions (verified/final-granted conversions), and earnings (after your app's payout split; USD). Returns rolled-up totals plus a per-day series (`daily`). Optional `startDate`/`endDate` (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC, inclusive; start must be <= end) filter everything; absent = all-time. Clicks attribute by transaction date; completions + earnings by completion date. An unknown creatorId returns 200 with empty campaigns/daily and zeroed totals. Authentication: publishable key (X-API-Key: pk_live_* / pk_test_*).

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency for every `earnings` figure. Always USD.

startDate.description: Echoed applied range start (YYYY-MM-DD), present only when supplied.

endDate.description: Echoed applied range end (YYYY-MM-DD), present only when supplied.

clicks.description: Distinct clicks in range (each click mints one transaction).

completions.description: Clicks whose transaction reached a completed status (verified / final_granted) in range.

earnings.description: Creator/publisher's earnings for this campaign in `currency`, after the app's payout split (raw payout sum if no split is set).

daily.description: Per-day series across all campaigns, ascending; days with no activity are omitted. Clicks attributed by transaction created_at (UTC); completions + earnings by completion timestamp (UTC).

get.description: Server-to-server only (HMAC; the signature covers the query string). Returns the link that sends this user back to an unfinished offer, or `claimUrl: null` with a `reason`. 404 unless the claim belongs to an app in your project (and, when `userId` is sent, that user owns it); a claim of an erased user is always 404, and a test key sees only claims made in a development environment. Leaving out `userId` skips the ownership check, so sending the link to the right user is up to you; a claim made before identify() keeps its pre-identify owner, so omit `userId` to reach it.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Your app user id that owns the claim. When sent, a claim owned by another user is 404. Leaving it out skips the ownership check, so making sure the link reaches the right user is up to you. A claim made before identify() keeps its pre-identify owner: omit userId to reach it.

parameters.name: transactionId
parameters.description: The claim's transaction id (the id the advertiser link carries).

claimUrl.description: The link that sends this user back to the offer, with their transaction id in it. Whoever opens it completes the offer as this user, so send it only to them and keep it out of logs. Null when there is no link; `reason` says why.

linkType.description: `advertiser`: the advertiser's own link, with no expiry set by Encore. More values may be added; any value still means `claimUrl` is a link.

expiresAt.description: When `claimUrl` stops working, if Encore sets an expiry. Null for `advertiser` links.

reason.description: Why `claimUrl` is null: `completed`, `revoked`, `closed`, `demo`, `campaign_inactive`, `not_per_user` or `no_destination`. Treat any other value as no link. Null when there is a link.

campaignId.description: The campaign this claim is for.

status.description: `open`, `completed` or `closed`. Treat any other value as closed.

isTestRequest.description: True when the claim was made in a development environment (a test key or a debug build).
